quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If an officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, what should drivers do?
questions.explanation: When a police officer is directing traffic, follow their directions instead of the traffic light. An officer's directions take priority over traffic signals.

questions.question: A pedestrian crosses after the "Don't Walk" sign flashes and is still in the street when your light turns green. What should you do?

options.text: Go ahead because you have the right-of-way.
Go ahead if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, you must let pedestrians finish crossing. Always give pedestrians time to clear the intersection safely before you proceed.

questions.question: When weather or darkness requires you to turn on your lights, what should you use?
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, or rain. High beams reflect off moisture and create glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: When turning left, drivers must yield to:
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming traffic. You can only turn when it is safe and you will not interfere with oncoming vehicles.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A road joins from the right.
The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you the road ahead will curve sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid losing traction on wet roads?
questions.explanation: Slow down on wet roads to prevent hydroplaning. Keep your tires in good condition. If you lose traction, ease off the gas, do not brake hard, and steer to maintain control.

questions.question: Your reaction time becomes slower after:
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes, reduces your vision, and makes you less alert. As you drink more, your judgment gets worse and your driving skills decrease. You will have trouble judging distance, speed, and other vehicles.

questions.question: When you have a green light and there are pedestrians in the intersection, what must you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way over pedestrians.

questions.explanation: Even with a green light, you must yield to pedestrians already in the intersection. Always let pedestrians cross safely before you proceed.

questions.question: Tailgating (driving too close to another car's rear bumper):

options.text: Prevents other cars from cutting you off.

questions.explanation: Tailgating is dangerous and can lead to aggressive driving. You can receive a traffic citation for unsafe driving.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and keep going at the same speed.
Speed up to get away from the area quickly.

questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians who might cross your path. If you see pedestrians near the road, slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly blows out while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of traffic.
Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of traffic.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, stay calm. Hold the steering wheel tight and take your foot off the gas. Let the car slow down on its own. Brake gently when safe. Do not move to the shoulder until the car has slowed down a lot.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They warn you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a steep hill is coming. Slow down and be ready to shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You are entering a one-way street in the wrong direction.
You can go if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are entering a one-way street in the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a one-way street or entrance. If you see this sign, traffic is moving toward you. Turn around if you are driving toward it.

questions.question: The posted speed limit should only be driven:
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest you can legally drive when conditions are perfect. It is safest to drive at the same speed as other traffic, up to the limit. All drivers must drive at a safe speed at all times.

questions.question: When a car with bright headlights drives toward you at night, you should:

options.text: Stop until the other car passes.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights at night because it can blind you. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes.

questions.question: When you are behind a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Keep a larger distance between your car and the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a larger distance between your car and the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Keep at least three to four seconds of following distance behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop fast, and following too closely is dangerous for you and the rider. If they fall, you need extra space to avoid them. Wet roads, ice, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridge grates increase the risk of falls.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: One outside mirror removes all blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can check blind spots by using your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Even with proper mirrors, all vehicles have blind spots. Large trucks have much bigger blind spots than most cars.

questions.question: What is the only effective way to remove alcohol from your body?
questions.explanation: Time is the only way to remove alcohol from your body. Eating, drinking coffee, or taking a shower will not speed this up.

questions.question: The amount of alcohol in the blood is called:
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. The higher the BAC, the more impaired you are.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog?

options.text: Honk your horn so they know to move.

questions.explanation: If you see a blind person crossing at a crosswalk or intersection, use every precaution and be courteous. Let them cross safely before you go.

questions.question: When a school bus is stopped ahead to load or unload children, what must you do?

options.text: Stop completely until all children have left the bus.
Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled in.
Change lanes and pass the bus slowly and carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled in.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights and a stop arm extended, you must stop completely. Do not drive until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled in. Even after the bus moves, wait to make sure no children are crossing in front of you.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Watch for traffic coming from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for traffic coming from the right.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs with black markings tell you about road hazards ahead. This sign warns you that traffic will be merging into your lane from the right.

questions.question: When rain or fog reduces visibility, drivers should use:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. Even if they do not help you see better, low beams help other drivers see your vehicle.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drugs and driving?

options.text: Prescription drugs are safe to use while driving if you do not feel drowsy.
Over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving ability.
Only illegal drugs can affect your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving ability.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs can make it harder to drive safely. These include drugs for colds, hay fever, allergies, and muscle relaxants. The law states you cannot drive while under the influence of any drug that affects your ability to drive safely—whether it is illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter.

questions.question: A school bus is stopped in your lane with red lights flashing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and continue when you think all children have exited the bus.
Slow to 25 mph and pass carefully.
Stop while the red lights are flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop while the red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop and stay stopped as long as the school bus has flashing red lights. You do not need to stop if the bus is on the other side of a divided highway.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Always let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first.
You have the right to go before oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Never let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first.
questions.explanation: When turning left at an intersection, let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first. Once the way is clear and the signal allows, you can complete your turn.

questions.question: Driving on the interstate requires drivers to:

options.text: Be able to safely drive at higher speeds.

questions.explanation: Safe interstate driving requires you to stay alert at all times and be able to drive safely at high speeds.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to be sure the lane is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to be sure the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure it is safe to change lanes.

questions.question: Use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days to:

options.text: Help other drivers see your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help other drivers see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: In rain, snow, or fog, other drivers have trouble seeing your vehicle. Headlights make your vehicle easier to see. If you need to use your windshield wipers, you must also turn on your low beam headlights.

questions.question: You can identify an aggressive driver by:

options.text: The number of passengers in their car.

questions.explanation: Watch other drivers while driving. If you see an aggressive driver making sudden or improper lane changes, do not challenge them. The safest action is to stay away from them.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Only look at the middle of the road.
Watch the sides, ahead, and behind your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the sides, ahead, and behind your car.
questions.explanation: Watch the sides, ahead, and behind your car. Good drivers know what is happening all around them.

questions.question: You can drive while taking medication that affects your driving:
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive while impaired by any substance. This includes alcohol, prescription drugs, over-the-counter drugs, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol or drugs from your system?
questions.explanation: Alcohol leaves your body slowly. Cold showers, black coffee, and exercise do not reduce blood alcohol content. Waiting is the only way to lower it.

questions.question: To see traffic behind you:

options.text: Turn and look out the back window.
Keep other cars out of your blind spots.

questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror often to know where traffic is behind you.

questions.question: You should drive on the shoulder to pass a car:

options.text: If the car ahead is turning left.
If the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.explanation: Never pass on the shoulder. The other driver will not expect you there and may pull onto the road.

questions.question: You want to turn right at a corner. A blind pedestrian with a guide dog is crossing in front of you. You should:

options.text: Turn off your engine until the person crosses.
Tell the pedestrian when to cross.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes always have the right-of-way.

questions.question: Which statement is true about changing lanes?

options.text: You only need to look over your right shoulder for all lane changes.
Look over your right shoulder for right lane changes and your left shoulder for left lane changes.
Cars with two outside mirrors have no blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your right shoulder for right lane changes and your left shoulder for left lane changes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal and check your mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and make sure the next lane is clear.

questions.question: Use your horn when:

options.text: Another vehicle is in your way.
It may help prevent a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may help prevent a crash.
questions.explanation: Only use your horn when needed to avoid crashes. Do not use it to make slow drivers go faster.

questions.question: A bad suspension can cause:
questions.explanation: Your suspension helps you control your car and provides a smooth ride. If your car bounces a lot over bumps or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: It is against the law to:

options.text: Pass in a marked no passing zone.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to pass in no passing zones, at railroad crossings, at street crossings, or where a solid yellow line is next to your lane. Do not pass in work zones or when the car ahead has stopped for a pedestrian.

questions.question: If you have an argument with another person and feel angry, you should:

options.text: Play the radio loudly while driving so you don't think about the argument.
Wait a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Drive on the interstate to release stress.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions affect your ability to drive safely. If you are very angry, excited, scared, worried, or sad, take time to calm down before driving. You need to focus on driving without thinking about what upset you.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, you should:
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop at the nearest rest stop or service area. You can nap, stretch, or let someone else drive. Caffeine pills and energy drinks do not replace rest and can make driving more dangerous.

questions.question: Blind spots are:

options.text: Areas in your vision that appear when you get tired.
Parts of the road you cannot see in your vehicle's mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts of the road you cannot see in your vehicle's mirrors.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder toward where you want to go. Check for objects near the rear corners of your vehicle. These areas are called blind spots because your mirrors cannot show them.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce road rage?

options.text: Talk on your cell phone while driving.

questions.explanation: To help prevent road rage, follow all traffic laws, signs, signals, and road markings. Always signal before you change lanes.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Pump the brake pedal several times quickly.
Slow down gradually and do not use the brakes.
Press hard on the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat while driving, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle straight. Remove your foot from the accelerator and do not brake. Let the vehicle slow down naturally. Use the brakes gently only if needed. Pull over safely when you can.

questions.question: When should drivers yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if pedestrians wave to you first.
Only if pedestrians are not texting while walking.

questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle completely at a crosswalk to let any vehicle or pedestrian already in the intersection pass. You may slowly go forward only if your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: Excessive speed:

options.text: Saves time and gets you to your destination faster.
Increases the risk of serious injury or death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of serious injury or death.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a common cause of vehicle crashes. It does not save time and often leads to poor driving decisions.

questions.question: Double solid yellow line markings mean:
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean no one can pass from either direction.

questions.question: If you drink several beers, alcohol's effects will wear off only by:
questions.explanation: Only time will reduce alcohol's effects in your body. Coffee, exercise, or cold showers do not speed this up. One drink takes about one hour for your body to process.

questions.question: The speed limit in school zones is:
questions.explanation: Unless a different speed limit is posted, you cannot drive faster than 20 mph in school zones. Always be careful when driving near children.
